title: Powers of the blooding
summary: Abilities unlocked by the warrior Salubri ritual.

claims.text: Only warriors who went through a true blooding according to the Code of Samiel gain its powers; corrupted versions of the rite unlock nothing.
Each power of the blooding costs 7 experience points.
Valeren is split into two paths, a structure otherwise seen only in Tremere Thaumaturgy.

title: Tracker’s Mark
summary: A blooding power that reads and follows spilled blood.

claims.text: With the prey’s blood on finger or tongue, the warrior rolls Perception + Awareness at difficulty 6; each success yields one fact such as generation, age, occupation or whether the target is a diablerist.
Tasting rather than touching the blood lowers the difficulty by 1, and the difficulty drops by another 1 for each generation the target stands above 8th.
Following a blood trail uses Perception + Survival at difficulty 6, each success covering one scene before a new roll.
Some warriors say blood that was stolen from their line burns or smells of rotting hay, which helps in tracking Tremere and Baali.

title: Blessing of the Name
summary: A blooding power that calls on the warrior’s angel.

claims.text: The warrior invokes the angel whose name the warrior bears, and the third eye opens to bathe everything in hard golden light that can terrify foes or rally a weary army.
Dirt vanishes and rusted armour shines; witnesses later agree only that they saw a marvel, never on what it was.

title: Peacemaker
summary: A healer’s power that calms a room.

claims.text: Under its aura even mortal enemies can talk through a dispute, and Brujah suffer +2 difficulty on rolls of aggression.
Anyone wishing to insult or lash out must roll Willpower at difficulty 8 or subside into confusion; gentle Natures are least affected.
It works best in a small room; two more Willpower points let it fill a hall or sanctuary as strongly, and afterwards some parties regret deals made under its influence.

title: King David’s Blessing
summary: Healing through music, also called Rayzeel’s Song.

claims.text: Rayzeel is said to have created it to lift Saulot from despair after the Baali Wars.
The healer sings or plays and rolls Charisma + Music at difficulty 7; each success lowers the difficulty of a following healing roll by one, to no lower than 4, or 5 against a Derangement.
Played to help another healer, each success adds a die to that healer’s roll, up to five dice.
Failure adds +1 to later attempts and a botch +2, may cause a level of damage, and can draw spirits that feed on discord.

title: Sword of the Righteous
summary: A Valeren power that sets a blade alight with holy fire.

claims.text: The warrior coats the blade in personal blood, taking a health level of damage, and rolls Strength + Occult at difficulty 7.
On success golden flames burn until the scene ends, adding two dice of aggravated damage and imposing +1 difficulty on anyone attacking the wielder.
Lesser powers of shadow cannot smother the flames.

title: Watching the Passage and Heaven’s Gate
summary: High healer powers tied to death.

claims.text: Watching the Passage lets a Salubri draw on the echoes left by someone who accepted Ending the Watch, merging with the spirit for a Willpower point and a Perception + Empathy roll; it can heal the Salubri but consumes the departed’s essence.
It works only within a week of the death, and a botch deals aggravated damage and may draw a hostile spirit.
Heaven’s Gate returns the soul to a body dead no more than ten minutes, for 2 Willpower and a Willpower roll at difficulty 8; unless the body is mended the person soon dies again.
Scent of the Other, a 1-point Merit, makes others slow to accept that the character is Salubri and quick to explain away odd behaviour.
Protected, a 2 to 5 point Merit, gives shelter from the Tremere hunt, ranging from a watchful mortal or ghoul to a powerful elder, a church or monastery with Faith, or a mortal lord and retinue.
Warrens is a 3-point Merit for hiding places; Sight Beyond Sight is a 5-point Merit for occasional visions through the third eye, and Visible Eye a 5-point Flaw for a third eye that will not close.
